name: Engineering Graphics & Design Lab
sem: I or II (group-wise; alternative to Workshop Practices Lab MEP-003)
objectives: Design a system, component or process to meet desired needs within realistic constraints such as economic, environmental, social, political, ethical, health and safety, manufacturability and sustainability.
Use the techniques, skills and modern engineering tools necessary for engineering practice.
Convert new ideas and design concepts into the basic line language of graphics using CAD software.
outcomes: CO1 Basic knowledge of engineering graphics using letter writing, different types of scales, lines and dimensions.
CO2 Draw orthographic projections of points, lines, planes and solids.
CO3 Understand the principle of isometric projection and develop isometric views by different methods.
CO4 Become familiar with AutoCAD 2-D and 3-D drawings and the various AutoCAD commands.
CO5 Use appropriate computer technology and work as a team.
text: N.D. Bhatt, Panchal V.M. & Ingle P.R., (2014), Engineering Drawing, Charotar Publishing House
M.B. Shah & Rana B.C. (2008), Engineering Drawing and Computer Graphics, Pearson Education
An Introduction To AutoCAD for Beginners by Autodesk
K.L. Narayana & P Kannaiah (2008), Text book on Engineering Drawing, Scitech Publishers
note: Marks 50 sessional + 50 external = 100 for the combined MEP-002/MEP-003 row (credit 2, L-T-P 0-1-2).

units.title: Introduction to Engineering drawing
formulas: RF = length of drawing / actual length of object
Plain scale reads units and primary divisions; diagonal scale reads up to three units
Lines: continuous thick (visible), thin (dimension/projection), dashed (hidden), chain (centre)
hints: Practise BIS lettering (5 mm, 7 mm) and line types on a sheet.
Draw plain and diagonal scales for a given RF.
Draw the three views of a simple block in first-angle projection.

units.title: Projection of points, lines, simple objects and conventions
formulas: Point above HP: front view above XY; in front of VP: top view below XY
True length of an inclined line = top-view length ÷ cosθ (θ = inclination to HP) = front-view length ÷ cosφ (φ = inclination to VP)
Line parallel to a plane shows true length on that plane
hints: Practise line inclined to HP and VP: find true length and true inclinations.
Draw projections of a point in all four quadrants.

units.title: Isometric and oblique views, Auxiliary Views, Development of surfaces
topics: Development of surfaces of simple solids
formulas: Isometric scale = cos 45° / cos 30° ≈ 0.816 (isometric length = 0.816 × true length)
Development of a right cone: sector angle θ = (r/l) × 360°, l = slant height
Development of a cylinder is a rectangle πd × h
hints: Draw an isometric view from given orthographic views.
Develop lateral surfaces of a prism, pyramid, cylinder and cone.

units.title: Orthographic and sectional views of simple assembly
formulas: Section lines: thin lines at 45° to the axis, equally spaced
Cutting plane shown by chain line thick at ends
Bolts, nuts and shafts are not sectioned longitudinally by convention
hints: Draw front view in section and top view of a socket-and-spigot or cotter joint.
Draw a muff or flange coupling in section.

units.title: Introduction to computer aided drafting
topics: Introduction to computer aided drafting in engineering drawing
Setting up and use of Layers
formulas: Layers group objects by line type, colour and lineweight
Common commands: LINE, CIRCLE, ARC, OFFSET, TRIM, EXTEND, FILLET, DIMENSION, HATCH
hints: Set up limits, units and layers, then draw a simple 2-D part with dimensions.
Plot to a scaled sheet using the Plot/Print dialog.
